//: Firebase Hosting config for the marketing site. Vite builds to dist/, so that's the public dir. The headers are the bandwidth lever — Vite emits hashed filenames (e.g. main-DM47416X.css), which means the file at a given path never changes content. Marking those immutable lets every returning visitor hit their disk cache instead of our $0.15/GB egress.

headers.//: Hashed bundles + the hero video — content is content-addressed by filename, so cache forever. `immutable` tells the browser to skip even the conditional-revalidation request.

Hero video specifically — same immutable treatment whether it lives under /assets/ (Vite-hashed) or /assets/hero.mp4 (direct reference). Belt-and-braces in case the build ever inlines references differently.

HTML entry points — must NOT be cached aggressively, or visitors keep loading old asset references after a deploy. `no-cache` here means the browser revalidates every time but can still serve stale on a 304.
Poster image and other root-level static assets — moderate cache since the filenames aren't hashed. One day is plenty for a marketing-site poster.
